A · Reading

1. A tax of 10 dollars for every traveller who leaves the country by plane, since the beginning of next year; i proceeds will go to the restoration of archaeological sites. The title contrasts two definitions given: investment (ministry) and jumping (opposition); The quotes indicate that they are words of the parties, not of the newspaper.

2. That said: the tax will not affect the number of tourists; many countries in the region apply similar or higher taxes ( ⁧قال⁩ , ⁧مؤكدا⁩ ). Avoided: whether the ministry has carried out an impact study; He said only that "the numbers speak for themselves" without mentioning any. Formulas: ⁧وردا على سؤال عما إذا⁩ … ⁧اكتفى بالقول⁩ … ⁧دون أن يذكر أي رقم⁩ . ⁧زعم⁩ points out that the journalist distanced himself from the opposition's argument (the tax would be just a leap to cover the deficit).
3. Probably ( ⁧على الأرجح⁩ ): the impact will be limited. Not excluded ( ⁧لا يستبعدون⁩ ): a decrease in short flights low cost, on which depends part of the domestic and regional tourism.

4. It was planned that the measure should be passed to Parliament before approval ( ⁧كان من المقرر⁩ ); on Government adopted it by decree. The opposition speaks of the distancing of institutions. the government spokesman denies: the law allows to impose taxes by decree. The newspaper speaks in the fifth paragraph: ⁧ولا شك أن ترميم الآثار ضرورة⁩ (the opinion presented as certainty); then reports the opinion given to experts on transparency.

5. That some users have posted a photo of queues at the airport doors, which would have been taken yesterday with reverse research it has emerged that it is of 2019 and another airport. Verdict: out of context (authentic photo, but of another time and place); misleading if used to claim that the tax creates queues.
B · Listening

1. The director of the capital's water company, on water disruption for a week. Certainty: the cause is a failure at the main pumping station, repaired yesterday; The water will return to all neighborhoods within two days. It does not exclude short interruptions in summer for the increase of consumption. Avoids the question if society knew the problem for months (it praises the question and changes theme).
2. Thesis: it is not necessary to ban phones at school entirely, but to teach a responsible use ( ⁧ليس⁩ … ⁧بل⁩ …).
Grant: it is true that the phone distracts pupils, but it can be a useful tool if used well. Proposal: Clear rules instead of a ban that no one respects.

3. On the closing of the streets of downtown on Friday. A man is favorable (people walk), but shops they must remain open; a woman is completely opposed, because she lives there and would not know how to get home in the car; A boy doesn't know, he hasn't tried yet: if it works well, otherwise they'll come back to the decision.

D · Translation

1. The spokesman for the ministry refused to comment on the news about an imminent resignation of the minister, It is simply said that the minister continues to work normally. 2. According to some analysts it is likely that the crisis will lead to early elections, although some of them do not exclude an agreement at the last moment.

3. The newspaper reported, quoting an informed source, that the negotiations are stalled, while the Ombudsman He denied, stating that concrete progress was made. 4. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs estimates the number of internally displaced persons in about two hundred thousand, while the humanitarian appeal is only funded for one third. 5. It is true that the reform has arrived late, but in our opinion it represents a step in the right direction. Accuracy points: in 1 ⁧رفض التعليق⁩ and ⁧مكتفيا⁩ ; in 2 two different degrees (probably / not excluded); in 3 the anonymous source, the denial, the quotation; in 4 estimation and financing; in 5 the concession; and ⁧في تقديرنا⁩ (The newspaper's opinion). An error on one of these points: Accuracy 3; two or more, or an error of meaning: 2.
